fix2:WS04-S4.summary: Both defects are fixed in model-gateway. Every requested command passed except the DB-gated session-core tests, which were not run because they need docker; no session-core file was edited, so nothing new there is untested. 1) gRPC ExitPlanMode now reads the run's own row (`read_run_detail` replaces `run_is_in_plan_mode`) when MODEL_GATEWAY_DURABLE_PLAN_GRANT is on. A `session_id` that differs from the run's `thread_id` is refused with PermissionDenied before anything is published, written or recorded. If the row cannot be read and a `session_id` is named, it answers Unavailable. The in-memory fallback is keyed on the run's own thread and is recorded only after a transient SetRunMode failure (Unavailable, DeadlineExceeded, Aborted, ResourceExhausted, Internal), via the new `coordinator::set_run_mode_failure_is_transient`. plan_approval applies the same rule; its key was already right (GetRun's thread). 2) For a waived credential, plan_approval now sends SetRunMode with the mode change alone: no rung, no justification, no plan id. The run leaves plan mode as before this slice. The answer says persisted:false, and with the flag on the approving replica keeps the grant in memory on the run's own thread. I chose the gateway strip because the waiver is readable from the HTTP claims. Session-core is untouched and keeps its refusal as defence in depth. No gRPC path needs it: authorize_request already refuses a waived identity on Write routes, so a waived caller never reaches gRPC ExitPlanMode. Two things to know. The strip means a waived approval no longer writes the runs.metadata autonomy_rung/justification copy. That follows the decision to strip granted_rung, but the review described that copy as part of the pre-slice behaviour. Also, the first lib run failed the zdr_posture raw-claim scan, so the waiver is read through the sanctioned adapter `zdr_posture::claims_view(&claims).waiver` rather than `claims.zdr_waiver`.

It answers Unavailable if the row cannot be read while a session_id is named. fix2:WS05-S4.summary:
All three defects fixed and proven. Every requested test command passes and the workspace check is clean (exit 0, no output). Mutations ran for defects 0, 1 and 2. No docker, commit, stage or push.

Defect 0 (retention-bound runs now learn built-in classes): in agent.rs merged_tool_defs_governed the resolve block was `if !zdr && (governed_mode != Off || gate != Off)`. It is now `if governed_mode != Off || gate != Off`. governed_mode is already forced Off for a ZDR or waived run (both reach the function as `zdr`), so such a run makes no MCP listing, puts no MCP name in the binding lookup and has no MCP prefetch. It still calls resolve_run_offer with MCP off and the built-in names when gate != Off, and records those views. The gateway token is minted only for the listing, so none is minted. The registry lookup uses the capability bearer and carries tool names only. With gate Off, a retention-bound run asks nothing. Tests in agent.rs: a_retention_bound_run_learns_a_tightened_built_in_class_like_any_other_run, a_retention_bound_run_under_a_gate_that_reads_no_class_asks_nothing. The three existing ZDR/waived tests now assert no MCP name reached any lookup, using a new FakeGoverned.asked_names recorder, instead of zero lookups. The ladder pin is a_retention_bound_run_still_learns_the_built_in_classes. The test refuses code_interpreter, declared external_write by the registry, at the read-only rung for a non-ZDR control run, a ZDR run, a waived run and a ZDR+waived run, each with MCP mode Off, Read and All. It also asserts 0 listings, exactly 1 lookup with no mcp__ name, no MCP tool offered and no prefetch.

Defect 1 (merge, not clear-then-fill): McpRegistry::replace_org now builds the incoming map, upserts every incoming server, then removes only the keys absent from the answer. It returns the removed ids. A catalog entry is dropped when the server is new, its config changed (url, transport, tool_allowlist, enabled, token; display name ignored) or the server is gone, and kept otherwise. New helper same_discovery_config. New apply_mcp_projection, which hydrate_mcp_registry calls: ownership.set for every entry first, then reg.replace_org, then ownership.remove for the removed ids. A present server is never missing from the registry or the sidecar at any instant. Tests: a_refresh_keeps_the_catalog_of_an_unchanged_server_and_drops_a_changed_or_removed_ones (through hydrate over HTTP; also checks ownership), only_a_change_to_what_discovery_depends_on_drops_a_servers_catalog (also covers orphan catalogs and other orgs), and a_reader_never_finds_a_server_missing_that_is_in_both_the_old_and_the_new_answer (3 spinning reader threads against 20,000 alternating refreshes through apply_mcp_projection).

Defect 2 (fail closed again): new clear_org_mcp_cache clears registry, ownership sidecar and discovery catalog. hydrate_mcp_registry now clears on a transport error, any non-success status other than 401/403 (5xx, 404, 429 and the like), an unparseable body, an empty registry URL and an invalid registry URL. It leaves the cache untouched on 401 and 403, and on an empty bearer (nothing was asked of the registry; that is a caller defect). A successful fetch replaces as before. Tests: a_bearer_capability_core_refuses_leaves_the_orgs_registry_intact (now 401 and 403, plus a blank bearer, then through mcp_tool_listing), a_registry_that_cannot_answer_clears_the_orgs_cache (500, 502, 503, 404, 429, garbled 200, unreachable host, empty URL, unparseable URL), a_failed_hydration_clears_only_its_own_org, and the existing a_successful_fetch_still_replaces_the_orgs_registry_with_the_registrys_answer. The old a_failed_fetch_leaves_the_orgs_registry_intact is removed because it asserted the opposite. I also updated the doc comment of forwarded_capability_bearer in grpc.rs (comment only; list_mcp_tools code is unchanged).

Mutations run, each restored and the passing state re-confirmed:
- Defect 0: put `!zdr && (...)` back on the resolve block. The ZDR case of the lib test failed ("the run did not learn the registry's class for the built-in tool") and the ladder pin failed.
- Defect 1: re-added inner.retain and catalog.retain at the top of replace_org. The two catalog tests failed ("an unchanged server lost its discovered catalog") and the concurrent reader test failed ("a present server was seen missing").
- Defect 2: made clear_org_mcp_cache a no-op. a_registry_that_cannot_answer_clears_the_orgs_cache and a_failed_hydration_clears_only_its_own_org failed ("a revoked server stayed callable").
- Defect 2 (401/403 exemption): replaced the status check with `if true`. The bearer test failed ("the registry row was dropped").

Line endings: agent.rs was CRLF in the working tree (HEAD stores it as LF), and between my edits and the first mutation script I found it had flipped to LF with no action of mine that explains it. I converted it back to CRLF (25821 CRLF of 25821 lines) before the mutation runs and tests. Whoever owns that file should check the line endings again. The other three files are all CRLF.

verdicts.evidence: Flag on: in grpc.rs exit_plan_mode, require_durable_run_owner runs first, then read_run_detail (GetRun with the caller's own session bearer). A non-empty session_id that differs from detail.thread_id returns PermissionDenied before handle_exit_plan_mode_durable, so nothing is published, written or recorded. If the row cannot be read and a session_id is named, the call answers Unavailable. The only fallback record_grant (grpc.rs ~1500-1507) is keyed on run_thread (detail.thread_id), and it runs only when coordinator::set_run_mode_failure_is_transient(code) holds (Unavailable, DeadlineExceeded, Aborted, ResourceExhausted, Internal), so a FailedPrecondition refusal keeps nothing. http_routes.rs plan_approval keys its fallback on GetRun's thread_id and keeps a copy only for a waived caller or a transient failure. The exploit chain the review described (own run R, name victim thread T, force SetRunMode to fail, get DANGER_FULL_ACCESS planted on T) no longer works with the flag on: it now ends in PermissionDenied. Tests an_exit_naming_another_conversation_is_refused_and_plants_no_grant, a_transient_durable_failure_keeps_the_grant_on_the_runs_own_thread, a_refused_durable_write_keeps_no_grant_in_memory and a_refused_durable_write_is_not_retried_and_keeps_no_grant all pass. One caveat, reported as a new defect: the same check is skipped with the flag off, which is the production default.

In http_routes.rs, set_run_mode_request_for(.., waived=true) sends mode 'execute' with granted_rung Unspecified and an empty justification and approved_plan_id. In session-core set_run_mode, refuse_waived_grant fires only on a stated rung, so this passes. With grant=None the grant_patch is {} and record_thread_grant is not called. The runs.mode update commits and nothing grant-shaped is written durably. persisted = durably_recorded = ok && !waived, so a waived approval answers false. Flag off: handle_exit_plan_mode keeps the in-memory grant, as before the slice. Flag on: the waived branch calls record_grant on GetRun's thread. `waived` is read from claims_view(&claims).waiver, the same raw claim presence session-core's zdr_waiver() tests. A waived identity cannot reach gRPC ExitPlanMode: authorize_request refuses Write on Route::plain with a waiver as a route mismatch, and a ZDR identity as durable_mutation_forbidden. The orchestration test a_waived_approval_updates_the_run_mode_and_states_no_durable_grant passes, for both flag settings.

new_defects.where: apps/Model Plane/rust/services/model-gateway/src/grpc.rs exit_plan_mode ~1422-1443 (run_detail is read only `if durable_grant`), feeding coordinator.rs exit_plan_mode ~610-612 `store.record_grant(&req.org_id, &req.session_id, ..)`, honoured by sse.rs resolve_autonomy_rung ~9249 `None => store.granted_rung(org_id, thread_id)`
new_defects.scenario: MODEL_GATEWAY_DURABLE_PLAN_GRANT is unset, which is the production default. User X in org O owns any run R and sends gRPC ExitPlanMode{org_id:O, run_id:R, session_id:<thread T of victim V in O>, granted_rung:DANGER_FULL_ACCESS, justification:'x'}. require_durable_run_owner checks R only. The new session_id-vs-thread check runs only with the flag on, so handle_exit_plan_mode records DANGER_FULL_ACCESS on (O, T) in this replica's memory and publishes RUN_PLAN_MODE_EXITED naming T. V's next run on T on that replica gets DANGER_FULL_ACCESS from store.granted_rung, and an execute turn on T would be honoured. This predates this slice; HEAD records on req.session_id the same way. But it is the one record_grant call site that is still not keyed on the run's own thread, and the fix this round built covers only the flag-on path. The attacker needs the victim's thread id.
new_defects.fix: Call read_run_detail regardless of the flag. Refuse a non-empty session_id that differs from detail.thread_id. When the row cannot be read, refuse whenever a session_id is named. Pass detail.thread_id, not the caller's session_id, into handle_exit_plan_mode, for example by overwriting req.session_id with it. Add a flag-off variant of an_exit_naming_another_conversation_is_refused_and_plants_no_grant.

new_defects.where: apps/Model Plane/rust/services/model-gateway/src/sse.rs with_local_fallback ~8880-8905 (memory is consulted only when Session Core holds no grant), combined with http_routes.rs plan_approval ~7845-7859 and grpc.rs ~1494-1507 (newest approval kept only in memory)
new_defects.scenario: Flag on. On thread T, user U approves danger_full_access and the grant is recorded durably, good for 24 h. A later plan-mode run on T is approved at read_only or workspace_write over a waived connection (deterministic: the waived SetRunMode states no grant, so Session Core's thread copy is untouched) or with a transient SetRunMode failure. That newest, narrower grant exists only in memory. On U's next run on T, durable_thread_grant reads Session Core's older DANGER_FULL_ACCESS, and with_local_fallback returns early because grant.rung.is_some(). The run executes at the wider, superseded rung. The durable approved_plan_id is the old, already-claimed plan, so the newly APPROVED plan is never offered either. Flag off, the newest approval replaced the previous one. The new comment says the waived run behaves 'exactly as it did before durable grants existed', which does not hold here. The approval answer reports the narrower granted_rung.
new_defects.fix: When memory holds a fallback grant for the thread, let it win over an older durable one. Either stamp the memory entry's recorded_at and compare it with a granted_at returned by GetThreadGrant, or at minimum take the narrower rung of the two together with the memory plan id. Alternatively, for a waived or failed write, explicitly clear or supersede the thread's durable grant in the same SetRunMode. A waived caller may not write one, but it could send an explicit 'revoke thread grant' that writes no content. Add a test: a durable DangerFullAccess, then a waived workspace_write approval, then the next run's rung.

new_defects.where: apps/Model Plane/rust/services/model-gateway/src/grpc.rs exit_plan_mode ~1448-1509 and http_routes.rs plan_approval ~7747-7765 (event published before the durable write), coordinator.rs exit_plan_mode ~621-657
new_defects.scenario: Flag on. Session Core refuses SetRunMode (FailedPrecondition, PermissionDenied, NotFound, InvalidArgument). This round's change means no grant is kept anywhere, but RUN_PLAN_MODE_EXITED has already been published with granted_rung, justification and plan_id, and the gRPC ExitPlanMode answers Ok(was_active:true). ExitPlanModeResponse has no persisted field. The audit stream then says a rung was granted that exists nowhere, and the gRPC caller cannot tell. Before this round a refusal left a memory grant, so the event was at least locally true.
new_defects.fix: With the flag on, publish RUN_PLAN_MODE_EXITED only after the SetRunMode outcome is known. Or publish a follow-up event, or carry a 'recorded' field in the payload, when the write was refused. Have gRPC ExitPlanMode surface a refusal of the durable write instead of answering Ok. Assert the published events in a_refused_durable_write_keeps_no_grant_in_memory.

new_defects.scenario: Flag on. SetRunMode fails with Code::Unknown, which tonic uses for some transport and h2 errors. plan_approval retries it 4 times as transient, then the keep predicate (set_run_mode_failure_is_transient, which excludes Unknown) keeps no memory copy. The plan is already APPROVED, which is single-use, so the grant the human approved exists nowhere and cannot be re-approved. This is the stranded-approval failure the retry was added to prevent. It fails closed: an availability and correctness inconsistency, not an authority one.
new_defects.fix: Use one predicate for both. Either add Unknown to set_run_mode_failure_is_transient, or drop it from set_run_mode_retryable, and have both call sites share the coordinator function.
